Vendor Stability.content:
Glean company overview
	•	Founded: 2019 by Arvind Jain and a team of former Google search engineers. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/about?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
	•	Operating history: Approximately 7 years (2019–2026).
	•	Business: Enterprise AI search and knowledge assistant platform. Glean connects company data sources and applications to provide AI-powered workplace search, answers, and agents. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/about?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
Funding rounds
Publicly reported funding:
Date|Round|Amount|Investors|
2022|Series B|~$100M|Sequoia Capital and others|
Feb 2024|Series D|$200M|Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners (co-leads)|
Sep 2024|Series E|>$260M|Altimeter, DST Global and others|
Reported valuation:
	•	Feb 2024: approximately $2.2B valuation. (Reuters("https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-enterprise-ai-search-startup-glean-raises-200-million-plans-hiring-spree-2024-02-27/?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
	•	Sep 2024: approximately $4.6B valuation after Series E. (Reuters("https://www.reuters.com/technology/ai-search-startup-glean-announces-new-funding-46-bln-valuation-2024-09-10/?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
Team size
	•	Glean announced plans in 2024 to double its workforce to around 700 employees after its $200M raise. (Reuters("https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-enterprise-ai-search-startup-glean-raises-200-million-plans-hiring-spree-2024-02-27/?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
	•	I did not find a current official headcount.
Layoffs / leadership departures
	•	I found no confirmed company-wide layoffs announced publicly.
	•	I found no major executive departures involving the founder/CEO.
	•	Founder and CEO Arvind Jain remains publicly associated with the company. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/about?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
Shutdown rumors / financial distress
	•	No credible reports of shutdown, insolvency, restructuring, or acquisition.
	•	Funding momentum and valuation growth indicate continued investor confidence. (Reuters("https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-enterprise-ai-search-startup-glean-raises-200-million-plans-hiring-spree-2024-02-27/?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
Assessment: Glean appears financially strong for an AI enterprise software company. The main risks are typical of high-growth AI startups: high valuation expectations, competitive pressure, and the need to convert enterprise adoption into durable revenue.

Incident History.content:
Data breaches
Confirmed customer data breach
No publicly confirmed Glean customer data breach found.
I found no reliable public disclosure of:
	•	stolen customer databases
	•	ransomware attacks
	•	unauthorized exposure of indexed enterprise content
	•	credential compromise caused by Glean
No vendor breach notification or major cybersecurity news report was found.
Evidence type: No confirmed incident found.

Major outages / service failures
I found no major publicly reported outage causing significant customer impact.
Glean does not appear to maintain a highly public incident history comparable to consumer SaaS platforms.
Potential reliability concerns discussed publicly are generally related to:
	•	connector synchronization
	•	indexing delays
	•	enterprise permissions configuration
rather than platform-wide failures.
Evidence type: No major public incident identified.

Security incidents / researchers
Enterprise data access concerns
Because Glean indexes sensitive company knowledge, security discussions focus on:
	•	permission inheritance
	•	access controls
	•	preventing overexposure of internal documents
These are architecture risks, not reported breaches.
Glean markets itself around permission-aware search, meaning access controls from connected systems are intended to be respected. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/platform/api?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))

Lawsuits related to data handling/security
I found:
	•	No major publicly reported lawsuits involving Glean alleging:
	◦	customer data misuse
	◦	privacy violations
	◦	security negligence
	◦	breach response failures
Incident History.source_type: self-reported (search found little; treat as thin coverage)

Data Handling Posture.content:
What data Glean collects and stores
Glean's product requires indexing enterprise information.
Potentially processed data includes:
Account/user data
	•	name
	•	email
	•	organization identity
	•	user permissions
	•	authentication information
Enterprise content
Depending on integrations:
	•	documents
	•	emails
	•	Slack messages
	•	knowledge-base content
	•	files
	•	metadata
	•	permissions information
The key function of Glean is building a searchable enterprise knowledge index.

Where data is hosted
Public information indicates:
	•	Glean operates cloud infrastructure for its SaaS platform.
	•	Exact cloud provider and regional hosting details are not fully visible publicly.
I did not find a complete public architecture document specifying:
	•	AWS/Azure/GCP usage
	•	exact storage regions
	•	backup locations
Assessment: Hosting transparency is more limited publicly than some enterprise SaaS vendors.

Data retention
I did not find a detailed public retention schedule covering:
	•	indexed documents
	•	logs
	•	backups
	•	analytics data
Enterprise customers likely receive more detail through contracts/security review.
Assessment: Retention policy: not fully public.

Does Glean use customer data to train AI models?
Glean states that customer data is used to provide enterprise AI functionality and integrates with models including OpenAI/Azure OpenAI. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/website-terms?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
Glean's terms state that when using Azure OpenAI/OpenAI through Glean's service:
	•	customer data is transmitted only when generative AI features are explicitly used
	•	negotiated zero-day retention applies for those services. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/website-terms?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))
I found no evidence that Glean uses customer enterprise data to train general-purpose models.
Assessment:
	•	Customer data used for retrieval/answer generation: Yes.
	•	Customer data used for general model training: No evidence found.

Subprocessors / third parties
Known categories:
	•	cloud infrastructure providers
	•	AI model providers
	•	enterprise integration providers
Glean may use:
	•	OpenAI/Azure OpenAI for AI functionality depending on configuration. (Glean("https://www.glean.com/website-terms?utm_source=chatgpt.com"))

Integration Risk.content:
lock-in|Medium|
Enterprise adoption switching cost|High|

Final assessment
Glean is a financially strong, rapidly growing enterprise AI company with no major publicly disclosed security incidents.
Strengths:
	•	strong enterprise search positioning
	•	impressive funding trajectory
	•	enterprise integrations
	•	permission-aware AI architecture
Risks:
	•	expensive enterprise pricing
	•	dependence on quality of company knowledge sources
	•	unclear public retention/hosting details
	•	moderate-to-high migration effort after deep adoption
The biggest lock-in factor is not the data itself; it is the enterprise knowledge graph, integrations, permissions model, and employee workflows built around Glean.
